challenges.name: coverage-vs-mutation-quiz
challenges.title: What do coverage and mutation score really say?
challenges.description: Compute a mutation score from a real-looking report, and decide which claims about node:test coverage are true.

questions.question:
A mutation run on src/coupons.js produced this report:

  mutants generated   20
  killed              14
  survived             6

The team reviewed the 6 survivors. Two of them change i < items.length to i !== items.length in a loop where i starts at 0 and goes up by 1 - they behave exactly like the original for every input. The other 4 are real gaps. What is the mutation score?
questions.explanation: Mutation score = killed / (total - equivalent). The two loop mutants are equivalent: no test can ever kill them, so they are removed from the denominator instead of being counted as failures or as successes. 14 / (20 - 2) = 14 / 18 = 77.8%. 70% (14 / 20) treats the equivalent mutants as gaps the suite should have caught, which punishes the team for something no test can do. 80% ((14 + 2) / 20) and 88.9% ((14 + 2) / 18) count the equivalent mutants as killed, which inflates the score: nothing in the suite actually caught them. The 4 real survivors stay in the denominator - each one is a missing test case.

questions.question:
Your project runs:

node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-coverage-lines=90

Which statements are true on Node 24? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Line coverage counts a line as covered when any part of it ran, so if (coupon.expired) throw new Error(...) on one line is covered by a test that only checks the condition - the throw never ran; branch coverage (and splitting the line) shows it. With --test-coverage-lines=90 the runner prints an error such as "77.78% line coverage does not meet threshold of 90%." and exits with code 1 even when every test passed, which fails the CI step. The report only lists files that were loaded while the tests ran: a source file no test imports does not appear at all, so it cannot drag the percentage down - it is silently missing, not 0%. And coverage records only that code ran; whether an assertion checked the result is invisible to it, which is why a suite of typeof checks can reach 100%.

options.text: A file can show 100.00 line % while a throw inside it never ran, if the if and the throw are on one line.
If line coverage is below 90%, the run exits with code 1 even when every test passed.
A source file that no test imports is listed with 0.00 line %, so it lowers the total.
100% line coverage means every line's result was checked by at least one assertion.

challenges.name: kill-the-surviving-mutants
challenges.title: Kill the surviving mutants
challenges.description: The shipping-fee suite reaches 100% line coverage, yet a mutation report lists seven surviving mutants and one equivalent one. Turn each survivor into a missing test case: the grader runs your shippingFeeSuite(shippingFee, assert) against the correct shippingFee, where it must pass, and against every mutant - including one that is not in the report - where it must fail.
